A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EASY-EP and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeepSeek-R1 pruning experiments, expert-activation analyses, ablations, and throughput measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3-0324, including additional benchmarks and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The main EASY-EP scoring formula and fixed-per-layer selection procedure remain unchanged. Appendix G.2 adds an experimental variant that normalizes scores within layers and ranks experts globally to allocate different expert counts across layers; this variant does not replace the recommended procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds USMLE and FinanceIQ evaluation and calibration data, expanding coverage from four domains to six. It also adds CommonCrawl calibration as a task-irrelevant input scenario and extends cross-domain transfer evaluation to medicine, finance, and agent tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds M-SMoE to both domain-specific and mixed-domain comparisons, expanding the evaluated alternatives from random and router-based pruning to expert merging. Random, Frequency, and Gating Score remain. The M-SMoE paper was cited in v1 but its method was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: v2 adds a complete DeepSeek-V3-0324 evaluation configuration. Appendix E changes the stated LiveCodeBench temperature from 0.6 to 0.2 and specifies a 1,000-example FinanceIQ evaluation subset. The main 25-shot calibration and 64-/128-expert configurations remain; the temperature revision alone does not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine expert overlap across depths and selection sizes, repeat localization and expert-removal tests using EASY-EP scores, compare selection metrics, and test variable pruning ratios across layers. Calibration-data analyses add CommonCrawl and DeepSeek-V3-0324. The component visualizations in Appendix D and longer-sequence throughput results in Appendix G.3 largely relocate existing analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports five evaluations per benchmark; v2 reports 32 for math benchmarks and five for most others. v2 also specifies FinanceIQ's subsampling seed. Both versions report mean pass@1 without adding confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises existing scores, including DeepSeek-R1's 128-expert AIME-24 result from 80.67 to 79.17, and adds extensive model, benchmark, and comparator results. New DeepSeek-V3-0324 results include Gating Score exceeding EASY-EP on 128-expert LiveCodeBench, 47.60 versus 46.71. Appendices add localization and variable-ratio findings. Revised settings and domain mixtures prevent treating aggregate differences as unchanged-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The expert-scoring definitions, cosine-based token weighting, output-norm bound, and perturbation-search complexity analysis are retained. Background equations are condensed or renumbered without substantive mathematical changes; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The main contribution remains few-shot domain-specific expert pruning with comparable performance at half the experts. v2 explicitly extends the headline claim to DeepSeek-V3-0324 and changes mixed-domain retention from approximately 95% to over 90%, while adding a claim of exceeding the full V3 model under mixed-domain pruning. These statements concern the expanded evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations concerning reasoning models' possible loss of long-generation capability, depth-dependent specialization, and communication-related throughput gains. It recommends mixed-domain pruning for multiple downstream tasks and fixed rather than variable layerwise ratios. Appendix A newly qualifies architectural generality and identifies post-pruning training and balancing domain capabilities as unresolved issues.

D1.justification: v2 adds calibration-set licenses, medical and financial calibration sources, FinanceIQ subsampling instructions, and the sample source for the representation-similarity visualization. It removes the abstract's code-availability statement and repository link. This establishes a loss of access information in the PDF, not that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds permutation-invariance and symmetry references to motivate neuron-misalignment concerns in expert merging, alongside sources for the added benchmarks. Several broader architecture and compression references disappear. The central positioning as efficient post-hoc, single-forward-pass pruning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses and rewrites the background, method explanations, and related work, merging the latter's two subsections. It reorders detailed analyses, incorporates throughput into that section, and redistributes explanations into expanded appendices. Terminology is standardized around few-shot expert localization.

P2.justification: v1's Figures 2–3 are consolidated into v2's four-panel Figure 2; the component visualizations move to Figure 8, and the former combined sensitivity/throughput figure is split. Table 2 gains model blocks and benchmark columns while losing the retention-ratio column. New appendix plots and tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The second-model evaluation, medical and financial tasks, merging comparator, and targeted appendix analyses strengthen the evidence beyond v1's single-model study; explicit limitations also improve qualification. However, v2 introduces unresolved reporting inconsistencies: its 64-expert R1 gating-only GPQA score is 46.83 in Table 2 but 20.20 in Table 3. Together with removal of the code link, these reporting and reproducibility regressions limit the net quality gain.
